::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-8}

I am an astrophysics researcher specialising in spectral line analysis and
pulling physical information out of large data sets. My current work, with
Dr. Kathleen Barger at TCU, uses integral field spectroscopy from the Local
Volume Mapper to study the gas in and around 30 Doradus, the largest
star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud. The spectra become maps:
one for every emission line, corrected for the dust in the way, and then read
together for what the gas is doing.

What I like most about the work is the part before the result: figuring out what
a data set can and cannot tell you, and building something that does not quietly
lie about its own uncertainty. I am at my happiest doing an in-depth
investigation into a data structure that nobody has looked at closely yet.

Outside of that, I am an enthusiastic karaoke singer, a gamer, and a traveler.

:::
:::

## Why this site exists

Two reasons.

<!-- HELD BACK (see .gitignore): the Research link below pointed at research/index.qmd -->
The first is ordinary: research should be findable, and code nobody can run is
not a contribution. The [Research](cv.qmd#research) section is where I write
up what I am working on and document the tools that come out of it.

The second is the one I care about more. I like taking high-level physics and
breaking it down to a level where anyone can actually engage with it — not a
watered-down version, the real thing explained properly. Most people who think
they are bad at physics have only ever met explanations written for people who
already understood. The [Teaching](teaching/index.qmd) section is my attempt at
the other kind, and it is free, permanently, to anyone who wants it.

## What I am working on

**Research.** Emission-line maps of 30 Doradus from LVM spectroscopy: dust
correction from Balmer decrements, then line-ratio diagnostics of the gas.
<!-- HELD BACK (see .gitignore): was [Read the project →](research/index.qmd) -->
[Read the summary →](cv.qmd#research)

**Teaching.** [Lab Help](teaching/labs/index.qmd), short answers for the
physics labs I teach, and *Python from Scratch*, a programming series for
people who have never written a line of code.
[Open the series →](teaching/python/index.qmd)

**Next.** Mathematics lessons and worked physics problems, both currently
outlined and not yet written.
